name: Traumatic Avascular Necrosis

criteria.description: Documented history of significant bone or joint trauma preceding symptom onset
Radiological evidence of bone ischemia and necrosis on MRI or X-ray
Localized joint pain and limited range of motion consistent with avascular necrosis
Exclusion of non-traumatic causes of avascular necrosis such as corticosteroid use or alcohol abuse

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of documented trauma history, imaging evidence of necrosis, and compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; biopsy rarely required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized joint pain exacerbated by weight-bearing

searchTerms: reduced range of motion in joints

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiological evidence of subchondral bone collapse
searchTerms: bone collapse under cartilage seen on x-ray
radiologic bone damage under joint surface
hard to move joints after inactivity
reduced joint flexibility especially in morning

common.symptomName: Limping or altered gait when lower limb involved
searchTerms: altered gait due to leg problem
walking difficulty from lower limb issue

common.symptomName: Tenderness on palpation of affected bone

occasional.symptomName: Muscle atrophy adjacent to affected joint
searchTerms: loss of muscle bulk by joint
joint fluid buildup on and off

occasional.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever
joint inflammation secondary to bone disease

laboratory: Exclusion of infection or systemic inflammatory disease
imaging: MRI showing bone marrow edema and necrosis
X-ray demonstrating subchondral radiolucency (crescent sign) and eventual bone collapse
CT scan for detailed bone architecture assessment
genetic: No known direct genetic mutations associated with traumatic avascular necrosis
other: Histopathology shows dead bone with empty lacunae and marrow necrosis if biopsy performed

distinguishingFeatures: Association with corticosteroid use or alcohol abuse

redFlags: Sudden worsening of joint pain with inability to bear weight
Signs of joint infection such as fever and erythema
Rapid progression to joint collapse or pathological fracture
references: Mankin HJ. Nontraumatic necrosis of bone (osteonecrosis). N Engl J Med. 1992;326(22):1473-1479.
Mont MA, Hungerford DS. Nontraumatic avascular necrosis of the femoral head. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1995;77(3):459-474.
